not_claimed: No novelty, hardness or speedup claim.

notes.result:
Can compact prime-field power-character predicates support a code-intersection
advantage after algebraic attacks, without hiding a random membership oracle?
This replaces more DCP barriers or polar mesh scans as the next constructive
test. The binary-extension accepted-flat attack does not automatically apply
to prime fields. That observation is NOT evidence of classical hardness.

The known quantum mechanism is dual-code list decoding plus Fourier readout.
[Sun-Wootters Theorem1.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12357#S1.SS2) states
prime-field OPI guarantees approaching SCL_rho(R), with perfect search for
fixed R+rho>1. Below R=1-rho, SCL is
`(sqrt(rho*(1-R))+sqrt((1-rho)*R))^2`; above it SCL=1, not the declining branch
of that expression. These are asymptotic guarantees with fixed positive
margins, NOT finite scores for our24 instances. Their random-oracle separation
does not transfer to our explicit predicates. No compiled coherent decoder
or finite success/gate certificate is supplied here.

The large-field decoder dependency matters: the
[Dao-Kominers-Thaler abstract](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2056) states
poly(n,log p) decoding at fixed capacity gap in sufficiently large characteristic.
Only its abstract was audited here, not its full proof or Lean development.
The [Jeronimo algorithm](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.05870) has polynomial
dependence on the field size in its stated decoder; that alone is insufficient
when log p, rather than p, is charged. A constant-gap finite implementation
must include uniform decoder synthesis and index-erasure/list-padding costs.

controls.heading: Constructive Classical Power Completion
controls.text:
For M selected common-coset positions, let T interpolate their shifts and
V=product(X-a_i). Set D=ceil(M/r), choose nonzero lambda and define

    W=lambda^r * X^(rD-M)*V,
    F=W-T/beta.

F has degree rD and leading coefficient lambda^r. In the formal series at
infinity, compute the polynomial part R of F^(1/r), of degree D. Then
`deg(R^r-F)<(r-1)D`. The code uses normalized reversed series, doubling Newton
precision and exact FLINT congruence/degree checks, not numerical roots.

    Q=T+beta*(R^r-W)=beta*(R^r-F)

has degree<(r-1)D and, at every selected point,
`Q(a_i)-t_i=beta*R(a_i)^r`. Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly
whenever `K >= (r-1)*ceil(N/r)`. This is a uniform constructive classical
explanation, not an inference from successful finite examples. At M<=K,
ordinary interpolation also works for arbitrary orientations because zero
residual is accepted. All final witnesses use independent Python modular
Horner evaluation, not just the formal-root implementation.

For lower rates one can force roughly rK/(r-1) common-coset constraints.
Under independent shifts at unseen coordinates the one-trial expected score
fraction approaches rho+R below the perfect threshold, with rho=1/r. It does
NOT match the published double-semicircle target throughout that region.
This expectation is neither worst-case, adaptive-attack nor best-of-restarts.
Do not call this an all-rate OPI dequantization.

controls.heading: Live Controls And What They Do Not Show
controls.text:
Twenty-four sources: six (p,N,K,r) configurations, seeds29/71, both modes.
Each r=2 source pays eight completion and eight jet trials plus one linear
baseline; higher r sources pay eight completion trials plus the baseline.
All344 native trial/baseline witnesses are retained, not just best successes.

At p=2^61-1, N127,K39, current global scores are108/110 and initial mixed
scores102/102. At N127,K77, global inputs are perfect and initial mixed
scores are118/118. The adaptive pass below improves the mixed witnesses.
Earlier fixed-leading jet trials scored120/118; releasing an extra leading

At N31,K16 mixed scores improve31/29 to31/30; global inputs are perfect. Common-coset

Missing a perfect mixed witness on one finite input does not imply classical

Neither best classical score nor a theoretical quantum mean is a matched
runtime/tail comparison. No positive candidate or active negative is admitted.

notes.decision:
- Common-coset high-rate perfect search is constructively classical both with
  zero included and, at one extra degree, with zero excluded. Do not keep
  varying seed, field size, power index or this zero convention as an escape.
- Mixed cosets may also be classically easy. The jet attack already exploits
  free coefficients overlooked by a straight formal-root test.
- Low-rate common-coset and mixed targets still lack matched quantum tails
  and stronger adaptive classical bounds. Failure of the current attack is
  only missing evidence, not a promising signal.
- The adaptive root-value falsifier is now implemented above. Its success
  does not prove a polynomial-time perfect mixed solver; its sampled stopping
  rule proves no lower bound against other attacks.
- A solver using simultaneous diagonal forms, algebraic elimination or
  rational approximants must return native affine witnesses and charge all
  setup/search. A homogeneous infinity point does not remove this blocker.
- A quantum proposal must provide the actual coherent capacity decoder and
  readout/resource analysis, or a different mechanism bypassing that dependency.

Tests exhaust1593 zero-including common-coset shift vectors at three small
thresholds,625 strict common vectors,625 mixed vectors for the free-jet degree
argument, all small diagonal roots including strict nonzero side conditions,
projective countercontrols, nontrivial cosets, Newton-vs-independent-square-root
series, search caps, adaptive monotonicity/full proposal replay, every saved
witness and deterministic artifact replay.
Passing these checks does not certify novelty or the asymptotic paper proof.

controls.heading: Classical Norm Construction
controls.text:
In the CONSTANT quadratic extension F_(p^2)=Fp[u]/(u^2-nu), an irreducible
over Fp splits into a conjugate pair exactly when its degree is even.
Odd-degree irreducibles stay inert. Thus a monic polynomial is a norm
exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity.

Factor F/rho^2 over Fp. Reject THIS target when an inert multiplicity is odd.
Otherwise factor over F_(p^2), choose one canonical member of each conjugate
pair, and half of each inert even multiplicity. Their product H satisfies
H*bar(H)=F/rho^2. Writing rho*H=R+uZ gives the required base-field norm.
Both extension and base-field polynomial identities are checked exactly.

These splitting/norm facts are standard, not a new algorithm claim; see
[Kuo-Liu-Totani](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ffa.2026.102812). The implementation
uses [FLINT finite-field polynomial algorithms](https://flintlib.org/doc/fq_default_poly.html),
not a home-grown factorization or a claimed quantum subroutine.

Finite-field factorization is randomized expected polynomial time in degree
and log p. Each trial also pays polynomial interpolation, exact products,
Frobenius conjugations and independent native Horner/membership verification.
The records charge base/extension factorizations and keep EVERY rejected
target. Those counters are not a complete bit/gate budget or a quantum
performance comparison. A bounded-search failure is UNKNOWN, not hardness.

notes.self_check:
The first implementation fixed rho=1. That restriction has an explicit
ALL-PARAMETER failure, even on a strictly easy input:

    p23,N8,K5,nu5,
    A={1,2,3,4}, B={5,6,7,8},
    t_A=(0,0,0,0), t_B=(19,22,8,6).

The constant Q=13 is a perfect STRICT solution. But D0=V_A-V_B has three
distinct linear roots0,9,16 and coefficients(0,4,14,16). Every monic-pencil
target is

    F_lambda=D0*(X/16-lambda).

The moving linear factor can make at most one fixed root's multiplicity
even. At least two inert multiplicities stay odd. Thus NONE of the23
parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy. The proof is algebraic;
the full23-case replay is an independent calibration, not the sole evidence.

The revised attack varies rho^2 as well. This removes that fixed divisor;
the counterexample now gets a perfect strict witness in5 paid trials.
For even |B|, gcd(V_A mod V_B,V_B)=1, and p>=5 supplies two different nonzero
square leading coefficients, so the expanded family has no fixed irreducible
divisor. Absence of a fixed divisor does NOT prove irreducibility, adequate
norm frequency or an inverse-polynomial success rate on every fixed input.
Odd-|B| auxiliary values introduce additional explicitly charged parameters.

bound, not an IID-input assumption. This does not certify the original61-bit
large examples or prove a general theorem for the smaller pencil below.

## Research Decision

The [previous prime-field experiment](PRIME_CHARACTER_OPI.md) solved common
cosets classically but left mixed high-rate controls at124/127 and122/127.
The new attack solves BOTH saved N127,K77 mixed inputs perfectly, including
strict nonzero variants, without changing their public shifts/orientations.
It does not apply to the saved K39 inputs under its degree budget.

There is also a useful mathematical result independent of those examples:
one trial has inverse-polynomial perfect-solution probability over an IID
uniform-shift population with suitable fixed orientations. That is a
population theorem, NOT a success bound for each fixed input or PRNG seed.

The quantum OPI guarantees and oracle separation in
[Sun-Wootters](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12357) are not refuted. Our predicates
are explicit translated power cosets, not random hidden membership tables.
This classical attack narrows which structured instantiations could support
a separation. A fixed-rate low-rate advantage remains unsettled.

## Problem And Exact Degree Budget

Input is the SAME public prime-field OPI specification: p odd prime, N<p,
evaluation points1,...,N, dimension K, public shifts t_i, orientations0/1,
and a verified nonsquare nu. Maximize acceptance of

    Q(a_i)-t_i in (Fp)^2             for i in A,
    Q(a_i)-t_i in nu*(Fp)^2          for i in B,
    deg Q<K.

The zero-inclusion convention is explicit. Strict mode requires every tested
root nonzero. No secret shift, field table, random oracle or acceptance-list
materialization is supplied. Modular exponentiation implements membership.
The reference inherits N<=4096 from the existing source. The arbitrary127-bit
prime cap was removed to execute the explicit Morse field regime; prime
validation remains. Exact large population counts use FLINT decimal rendering
instead of Python's limited decimal-int conversion. Operational limits are
not evidence of hardness or assumptions of the algebraic/population proof.

Interpolate T_A(a_i)=t_i on A and V_A=product_(i in A)(X-a_i). Choose public
lambda and nonzero rho, and set Q0=T_A+lambda*V_A. On B interpolate
F0(a_i)=t_i-Q0(a_i). If |B| is odd, include point0 with an independently
chosen auxiliary value, padding the interpolation to even size

    D=|B|+(|B| mod2).

Let V_B vanish on these B/auxiliary points and put F=F0+rho^2*V_B. Seek

    F=R^2-nu*Z^2,                  Q=Q0+R^2.

Then Q-t_i=R(a_i)^2 on A and Q-t_i=nu*Z(a_i)^2 on B. Both groups are
accepted if zero is included. The exact sufficient degree condition is

    K>max(|A|,D).

The norm factors have degree<=D/2, so this budget is verified BEFORE search.
The auxiliary point is part of a public algebraic construction, not a new
oracle problem or a replacement of any native constraint.

## Classical Norm Construction

In the CONSTANT quadratic extension F_(p^2)=Fp[u]/(u^2-nu), an irreducible
over Fp splits into a conjugate pair exactly when its degree is even.
Odd-degree irreducibles stay inert. Thus a monic polynomial is a norm
exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity.

Factor F/rho^2 over Fp. Reject THIS target when an inert multiplicity is odd.
Otherwise factor over F_(p^2), choose one canonical member of each conjugate
pair, and half of each inert even multiplicity. Their product H satisfies
H*bar(H)=F/rho^2. Writing rho*H=R+uZ gives the required base-field norm.
Both extension and base-field polynomial identities are checked exactly.

These splitting/norm facts are standard, not a new algorithm claim; see
[Kuo-Liu-Totani](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ffa.2026.102812). The implementation
uses [FLINT finite-field polynomial algorithms](https://flintlib.org/doc/fq_default_poly.html),
not a home-grown factorization or a claimed quantum subroutine.

Finite-field factorization is randomized expected polynomial time in degree
and log p. Each trial also pays polynomial interpolation, exact products,
Frobenius conjugations and independent native Horner/membership verification.
The records charge base/extension factorizations and keep EVERY rejected
target. Those counters are not a complete bit/gate budget or a quantum
performance comparison. A bounded-search failure is UNKNOWN, not hardness.

## Strict Roots Without A Field-Size Search

If F vanishes at any native point, nonsquareness forces R=Z=0 there. Reject
that strict norm TARGET, not the original OPI problem. Otherwise multiply
R+uZ by the norm-one Cayley element

    alpha_s=(1+s*u)/(1-s*u)=a_s+b_s*u,
    a_s=(1+nu*s^2)/(1-nu*s^2), b_s=2s/(1-nu*s^2).

The denominator never vanishes in Fp. Rotate

    R'=a_s*R+nu*b_s*Z,       Z'=b_s*R+a_s*Z.

The norm and degree budget stay unchanged. Each forbidden R'(a_i)=0 on A
or Z'(a_i)=0 on B has a NONZERO quadratic numerator in s, since the original
pair is nonzero. At most2N parameters are forbidden. For p>2N, one of
0,...,2N works. This is a deterministic polynomial-size candidate set, not
a full-field scan when p is large. Every actual rotation is stored and checked.

## Try To Disprove The Pencil, Then Repair It

The first implementation fixed rho=1. That restriction has an explicit
ALL-PARAMETER failure, even on a strictly easy input:

    p23,N8,K5,nu5,
    A={1,2,3,4}, B={5,6,7,8},
    t_A=(0,0,0,0), t_B=(19,22,8,6).

The constant Q=13 is a perfect STRICT solution. But D0=V_A-V_B has three
distinct linear roots0,9,16 and coefficients(0,4,14,16). Every monic-pencil
target is

    F_lambda=D0*(X/16-lambda).

The moving linear factor can make at most one fixed root's multiplicity
even. At least two inert multiplicities stay odd. Thus NONE of the23
parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy. The proof is algebraic;
the full23-case replay is an independent calibration, not the sole evidence.

The revised attack varies rho^2 as well. This removes that fixed divisor;
the counterexample now gets a perfect strict witness in5 paid trials.
For even |B|, gcd(V_A mod V_B,V_B)=1, and p>=5 supplies two different nonzero
square leading coefficients, so the expanded family has no fixed irreducible
divisor. Absence of a fixed divisor does NOT prove irreducibility, adequate
norm frequency or an inverse-polynomial success rate on every fixed input.
Odd-|B| auxiliary values introduce additional explicitly charged parameters.

## A Rigorous One-Trial Average-Case Statement

Assume truly IID uniform shifts, fixed orientations satisfying the degree
budget, and trial/auxiliary parameters independent of those shifts. Condition
on ALL A shifts and lambda,rho. The B values t_i-Q0(a_i) remain independent
uniform. If padding is needed, its independent uniform auxiliary value supplies
the remaining coordinate. Interpolation is a linear bijection, so F/rho^2
is a uniform monic degree-D polynomial.

Every irreducible degree-D polynomial works: D is even, so it splits in the
quadratic extension. It has no Fp root, also licensing strict Cayley avoidance
when p>2N. Therefore first-trial success is at least

    I_p(D)/p^D,       I_p(D)=(1/D)*sum_(d|D) mobius(d)*p^(D/d).

The producer records this EXACT rational population lower bound. For the
two saved orientation patterns D=58 and64, it is approximately1/58 and1/64.
These numbers are NOT probabilities certified for those particular saved
shifts. Seeded replays are not IID-source certificates. `attack(...,seed=None)`
uses system randomness under the usual uniform-bit assumption; producers
use explicit fixed seeds for deterministic replay.

For p>2N the elementary irreducible-count bound gives at least1/(2N).
With independent fair orientations and fixed rate K/N>1/2, the degree budget
holds with probability approaching1 exponentially fast; e.g. it suffices
that both groups have size<=K-2, an ordinary binomial-tail condition.
Thus the structured IID-shift high-rate population does NOT have negligible
classical perfect-solution success. This is NOT a high-probability or worst-
case classical solver, nor a dequantization of general OPI/oracle inputs.

Do not amplify this into a per-instance guarantee. Even independent trial
coins do not let one replace q(input) by its population mean in
E_input[(1-q(input))^T]. The fixed-monic counterexample illustrates the danger.
An argument about correlations or fixed-instance norm frequency is still
needed. Expected polynomial factorization work can be truncated at a
polynomially larger budget while preserving inverse-polynomial population
success; the prototype counters themselves are not a certified bit bound.
Subtracting a random degree<K polynomial from all shifts is NOT a free
worst-case-to-IID reduction: it preserves the N-K RS syndrome coordinates
and moves only within a K-dimensional orbit, not all Fp^N shift vectors.

## Executed Evidence And Decision

The unchanged N127,K77 seeds29/71 now have perfect127/127 classical witnesses
in1 and15 paid expanded-pencil trials. Both zero-including and strict versions
are retained. Their degrees69 and64 respect the predeclared K77 bound. The
same-input test checks specifications against the ORIGINAL source artifact.
Saved K39 siblings are NOT APPLICABLE, not declared hard or unsatisfiable.

Tests independently verify polynomial products/native Horner witnesses without
new factorization, exhaustively compare norm representability through degree4
over F3, check the all-parameter counterexample, and enumerate the121 B-shift
sources over F11 in the degree2 strict calibration. Exactly55 irreducible
targets yield perfect strict witnesses, matching I_11(2)/11^2=55/121.

Next high-value mathematics: establish or falsify useful fixed-input norm
frequency for the expanded family, with its exceptional pencils and actual
field-size requirements, OR find a genuinely lower-rate mechanism. Do not
replace that problem with more seeds, trial budgets or a claim that random-
polynomial statistics already prove a fixed-pencil theorem. No new central
candidate/negative/proof is promoted. Application remains REVIEW PENDING.

# Constructive Polar Gibbs Falsifier: No Free Source Table

2026-10-17. Known polarization, SC shaping and channel-duality mechanisms.
Local application and finite information-order certificates require review.
No novel quantum algorithm, all-code no-go or matched runtime advantage.

## Question And Decision

The preceding [polar sampler](POLAR_CONDITIONAL_SAMPLER.md) left an explicit
blocker: its average-case error criterion did not construct an appropriate
public code without an exponential source table. This pass removes that
blocker for concrete non-prefix families.

The signs model is not optional bookkeeping. [Zhou et al., Theorem 2.4 and
Theorem 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.40345v1#S2) use uniform random clause
signs and bound expected total variation. Their theorem does not supply
an arbitrary-sign guarantee. Thus the classical average-sign bound addresses
the actual proposed reduction, not an artificially weakened comparison.
It does NOT refute their random-hypergraph results: our code family is polar.

## Input, Mechanisms And Costs

Public input: power-of-two length N, rational overlap c, explicit polar
coordinate set F, and uniform public signs J. Set p=(1-c)/2 and let H_F
extract the selected polar coordinates. The task is sampling the kernel
word y with

```
H_F y=0,
weight(y) = product_j (1+c*(-1)^(y_j+J_j)).
```

Free polar coordinates of G(y) give the independent Ising spins in another
O(N log N) binary transform. The number of spins is N-|F|. A dense parity
matrix is polynomially expandable from N,F; no coherent access oracle or
unknown coefficient is provided. These interactions need not be sparse or
bounded-locality, and no random-LDPC/ER hardness claim is transferred to them.

Quantum proposal: known polar CQ successive cancellation, coherently used
inside the known DQI Gibbs reduction. Its synthesized message graphs avoid
the enormous LDPC extrinsic-tree issue. Good fidelity-based information sets
are a constructive decoding route, not a new algorithm or established
speedup. Reversible reliability arithmetic, retained workspace and the whole
Gibbs readout would still need to be charged.

Classical competitor: SC source shaping from the existing producer. It needs
only N,F,c,J, exact rational prefix probabilities and ordinary random bits.
It uses O(N^2) rational operations in this reference, not an exponential
source table. Rational numerator/denominator lengths are polynomial in N
and the input probability precision. Matrix/check generation and binary
transforms are additional charged work, not part of the rational counter.
Construction below costs O(N G^2) support-pair operations for G grid intervals,
plus polynomial-bit integer arithmetic. This is NOT a fine-grained matched
quantum/classical gate comparison or a claim of the best classical runtime.

## The Direct Decoder-Sampler Link

For source U=G(E), E_i IID Bernoulli(p), put

```
m_i = E |P(U_i=0 | U_<i) - P(U_i=1 | U_<i)|.
epsilon_F = (1/2) sum_(i in F) m_i.
```

The preceding hybrid argument gives average uniform-sign Gibbs TV at most
2 epsilon_F = sum_F m_i. There is no factor 2^|F| in this AVERAGE guarantee;
that factor arises only when trying to infer an arbitrary-syndrome bound.

The full posterior-magnitude laws have an exact recursion. For independent
child magnitudes a,b, an even source bit has magnitude ab. The odd source
bit has magnitudes (a+b)/(1+ab) and |a-b|/(1-ab), with branch weights
(1+ab)/2 and (1-ab)/2. The zero-probability a=b=1 branch is omitted.
Independence follows from the two disjoint source halves, not cloned data.

These are the same flagged pure-state channel combinations as BPQM, with
source/CQ indices reversed. In particular m_i equals the UNSQUARED root
Uhlmann fidelity of the reversed synthesized CQ bit-channel. Independent
small density matrices now verify this stronger identity, not just entropy:
root fidelity is computed from a purification-Gram nuclear norm, avoiding
spurious square roots of tiny numerical eigenvalues. Native N2/N4 errors
are below 3e-16; numerical checks are not formal theorem proofs.

Consequently, any polar Gibbs proposal whose justification is a vanishing
SUM OF THESE ROOT FIDELITIES also supplies this polynomial classical
average-sign sampler. A claim of a Shor-like separation cannot rest solely
on that criterion. This does not cover arbitrary joint receivers or every
weaker/different decoding-error criterion. No new channel-duality theorem
is claimed; see [Renes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05583) and the
[BSC/PSC treatment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.09225).

## Certified Finite Construction

Use overlaps m_j=j^r/G^r, j=0,...,G, and exact normalized dyadic herald
masses with denominator 2^b. The nonuniform mesh is important: a uniform
overlap mesh rounds every tiny nonzero magnitude up to at least 1/G,
which can make sum_F m_i vacuous at useful block lengths.

Each independent parent pair is combined EXACTLY in integer arithmetic.
Round resulting overlaps UP on the mesh. Round each herald mass down to
the dyadic lattice, replacing the discarded mass with overlap-one states.
All discarded mass is retained in the accounting; no renormalization hides it.
The computed mean overlaps are therefore upper bounds on the true m_i.

Why the bound survives repeated combinations: this is PHYSICAL PSC
degradation, not first-order stochastic ordering of posterior magnitudes.
If 0<=a<=d<=1, the two-state Gram identity permits the map

```
|psi_x(a)> -> |psi_x(d)> tensor |psi_x(a/d)>,
```

followed by discarding the environment (with the zero endpoint treated
separately). Removing herald mass to an uninformative overlap-one flag is
also a degrading channel. Product and averaged channel combinations preserve
this order, and root fidelity cannot decrease under degradation. The lower
comparison uses the reverse information order. This is a mathematical
comparison, NOT permission to erase environments inside a coherent receiver.

An explicit test shows why a scalar shortcut would be wrong: plus-combining
(a,b)=(0.1,0.9) versus (0.5,0.9) gives crossing posterior-magnitude CDFs.
Neither ordinary stochastic ordering nor mean-only rounding proves the
recursive certificate. Native exhaustive source controls and the previous
uniform-grid integer implementation independently check the nonuniform code.
Bounded-alphabet construction has substantial prior art, including
[Tal and Vardy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.6164); this is not claimed to be
their exact merge algorithm or a better construction theorem.

Select F by the smallest certified means. The report retains ALL N upper
bounds, F itself, the grid, exact masses' precision, pair/rounding work and
producer/helper hashes. It also retains failed target designs. The reported
maximum set size is maximum for THIS bound vector and TV budget, not the
optimal polar code or a capacity upper bound.

## Live Outcomes

At c=13/20, p=7/40, coarse G=64,r=4,b=96:

| N | Largest set certified at average TV<=0.1 | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | 16 | 0.25 |
| 256 | 78 | 0.304688 |
| 1024 | 361 | 0.352539 |
| 4096 | 1614 | 0.394043 |

The half-rate targets in these coarse controls all FAIL certification.
Their status is UNKNOWN at this resolution, not hardness or impossibility.
A clearly labelled post-exploration rate3/8 follow-up at N4096 has certified
average TV<=0.023431. It is non-prefix and exceeds the product-USD code-rate
ceiling 1-c=0.35. That ceiling is only for the specified full-rank product
USD/Prange mechanism, not all classical algorithms; this sampler is itself
a stronger classical algorithm. The certificate is not a quantum advantage.

The larger G=256,r=3,b=96 calculation succeeds at N32768, |F|=16384:

```
average uniform-sign Gibbs TV
 <= 424553765284920852120940002337825
    /41538374868278621028243970633760768
 < 0.010221.
```

It uses 65,534 channel combinations and 1,008,335,816 active support-pair
visits. The expensive setup is disclosed, not treated as free advice. The
initial exploratory run was repeated to save the full reproducible artifact.
This finite result removes the missing public-set construction premise for
the stated half-rate family. It does NOT prove a fixed-grid asymptotic
convergence theorem, a general Gibbs sampler, or an all-sign result.

An actual N1024,361-constraint non-prefix Gibbs sample is executed and its
native kernel checks are verified. The reference accepts lengths through
32768, but a 32768-bit Gibbs draw has NOT been executed; its polynomial
O(N^2) exact-arithmetic sampler can be expensive. Large-bound verification
checks provenance, all upper-bound arithmetic and selected-set sums, not
another billion-pair replay inside each unit-test run. That distinction
must remain explicit. Full-law TV is independently checked only on small
native sources; general validity rests on the stated review-pending proof.

## Execute And Falsify

```
python theorems/polar_conditional_sampler.py --write
python theorems/polar_source_design.py --write
python theorems/polar_source_design.py --length 32768 --grid 256 --power 3 --write
python -m pytest tests/test_polar_conditional_sampler.py tests/test_polar_source_design.py -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
```

The parameterized command writes a separate parameter-labelled artifact;
it does not overwrite the coarse failures. Reject this certificate if an
independent exact source calculation exceeds an upper bound, if physical
degradation/duality does not apply, if the source uses the coherent flip
probability gamma instead of p, or if future frozen information is uncharged.
An adversarial sign regime requires a different proof, not this average bound.

## Research Decision

Do not compile another natural SC-fidelity polar receiver to argue a
random-sign Gibbs advantage: the matching classical route is now constructive.
Do not extend mesh/block-size scans as the next research project. A next
pass must identify a genuinely different efficient quantum receiver/code
mechanism that escapes this classical sampler, or pivot independently.
Random LDPC/cyclic composition, arbitrary-sign sampling and non-SC joint
measurements remain unresolved; no barrier for those is established here.

# Polar Conditional Sampling Before Another Quantum Decoder

2026-10-17. Known SC/source-shaping mechanisms. Local Gibbs mapping, hybrid
bound and convention-specific entropy derivation require review. No new
quantum algorithm or general dequantization theorem is claimed.

FOLLOW-UP: [certified source design](POLAR_SOURCE_DESIGN.md) now constructs
an explicit non-prefix half-rate set without the exponential source table,
with average-sign TV<=0.010221 at N32768. It resolves the missing public-set
premise below for that finite family, not the worst-sign or all-code problem.

## Why This Direction Was Selected

The cubic OPI and native tail passes are complete. Rather than extending
their seed/degree scans, this pass examined a constructive alternative to
the enormous LDPC extrinsic trees and failed cyclic BPQM shortcuts: polar
successive cancellation (SC). Its synthesized message graphs are trees even
when the code has no tree Tanner graph. This is established prior art, not
our proposed new decoder: [Piveteau and Renes, Section 7.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.08170),
and [Mandal, Brandsen and Pfister](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.07167).

Before compiling such a receiver, test the strongest relevant classical
competitor: SC shaping for the dual source distribution. The question is
whether it solves the SAME signed code-Gibbs task, and whether correctness
holds on average or for every sign pattern.

## Input And Native Task

Let E contain N independent Bernoulli(p) bits, p=(1-c)/2, with rational
0<=c<1. N is a power of two. The public involutory polar transform gives
U=G(E). A public subset F of polar coordinates and a syndrome s impose
U_F=s. All matrices, constraints and probabilities are explicit.

Let H_F have rows giving these polar coordinates as parities of E. Given
arbitrary public clause signs J, set s=H_F J and y=E xor J. Then

```
H_F y = 0,
Pr(y) proportional to product_j(1+c*(-1)^(y_j+J_j)).
```

This is the native signed parity-Ising Gibbs law on the kernel of H_F,
not an oracle problem or a decoded-word proxy. A basis of this kernel maps
words bijectively to independent Ising spin coordinates. Tests compare this
identity against direct native weights for EVERY length-4 sign pattern.
The overlap c=13/20 corresponds here to p=7/40; it must not be confused with
the different bit-flip amplitude parameter used inside the coherent source.

values; sample other coordinates from the EXACT unrestricted-source

and diagnostic tables are SEPARATE and charged as exponential calibration.
Neither hidden frozen-set construction nor free probability tables are used.

constraint, so sampling is EXACT for every syndrome and sign pattern.
A fair source p=1/2 is also exactly handled for every subset F. These are

constraint masks, not just a plausible noise word or its energy.

## Average-Syndrome Guarantee, Not A Worst-Case Guarantee

Write

```
epsilon_F = sum_(i in F) E_(P prefix) |P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2|.
Qjoint(u) = 2^(-|F|) * product_(i not in F) P(u_i|u_<i).
```

A reverse-order hybrid replaces each frozen conditional by a fair bit.
Earlier prefixes still have their P distribution; later conditionals sum to
one. Thus TV(P_U,Qjoint)<=epsilon_F. The syndrome marginal discrepancy
delta=TV(P_(U_F),Uniform) is at most that joint discrepancy. Triangle
inequalities then give BOTH

```
E_(uniform s) TV(Q_s,P_(U|U_F=s)) <= epsilon_F+delta <= 2 epsilon_F,
E_(native s)  TV(Q_s,P_(U|U_F=s)) <= epsilon_F+delta <= 2 epsilon_F.
```

For a specific syndrome the resulting generic bound has an extra factor
2^|F|. Uniform clause signs give uniform syndromes because H_F has full row
rank, so the first average is exactly the uniform-sign Gibbs comparison.
There is NO claim that every adversarial sign pattern is handled well.

Entropy interpretation: Pinsker and Jensen give
E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2| <= sqrt((ln 2)/2 * (1-H(U_i|U_<i))).
Consequently a supplied high-entropy set with sufficiently small summed
entropy defects gives an average-case classical approximation. Standard
source polarization supplies such regimes; efficiently constructing and
certifying the PARTICULAR public set remains a charged obligation.
Relevant source-shaping prior art includes
[Zhao and Li, Appendix A / Corollary 17](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09239v2#A1),
which concerns averaged quantization noise, not automatic arbitrary-syndrome
conditional correctness. No new source-coding theorem is claimed here.

## Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal

For the pure-state channel
|psi_x>=sqrt(1-p)|0>+(-1)^x sqrt(p)|1>, overlap is c=1-2p.
Fixing a polar input prefix and averaging the remaining inputs dephases
the channel state into orthogonal character blocks. Its eigenvalues are
the probabilities of the source parities associated with the remaining
encoder rows. Subtracting consecutive state entropies gives the synthesized
CQ Holevo information. In the implemented convention G^T=R G R, with R
reversing coordinates. Hence the CQ information at i equals the source
conditional entropy at N-1-i. Small density matrices independently verify
this identity; they are not used as a decoder or scalable access primitive.
General channel/code duality is known: [Renes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05583),
with [a semiclassical BSC/PSC treatment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.09225).

Therefore the natural high-information polar receiver and high-entropy SC
shaping competitor are not unrelated constructions. If the corresponding
source set has epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction, a claimed
uniform-random-sign Gibbs advantage is removed by this classical algorithm.
That is a CONDITIONAL, review-pending application of known mechanisms,
not a worst-case-sign no-go, not all codes, and not a result established
by the small numerics. It warrants checking this competitor before spending
main-model effort compiling a quantum polar receiver.
